\section*{Methods}

\subsection*{Anatomical preprocessing}

\subsubsection*{Anatomical references}

For each participant, one T1-weighted (T1w) and one T2-weighted (T2w) reference were selected from all available sessions. The earliest acquisition of each modality was used. When no T1w image was available, a 1 mm T1w-like reference was synthesized from the T2w image with SynthSR \citep{iglesias2023synthsr}.

\subsubsection*{Intensity and gradient correction}

Each source image was corrected for gradient nonlinearity with the Human Connectome Project (HCP) gradient-unwarping procedure \citep{glasser2013minimal} when a site gradient profile matched the acquisition and its metadata did not report prior correction. A brain mask was estimated on each image with SynthStrip \citep{hoopes2022synthstrip}, and intensity nonuniformity was corrected within that mask with ANTs N4BiasFieldCorrection \citep{tustison2010n4itk}.

\subsubsection*{Reference alignment}

The T1w reference was rigidly aligned to the pose of the MNI152NLin2009cAsym template \citep{fonov2011mni} with ANTs mutual-information registration \citep{avants2011ants}. It was resampled once with cubic B-spline interpolation onto a template-oriented grid at the source resolution, and its brain mask was resampled with nearest-neighbor interpolation. When a T2w reference was available, it was aligned to the T1w reference with six-degree-of-freedom FSL FLIRT \citep{jenkinson2001flirt}.

\subsubsection*{Surface reconstruction}

Cortical surfaces were reconstructed from the T1w reference with FreeSurfer \emph{recon-all} \citep{dale1999cortical,fischl2012freesurfer}. FreeSurfer skull stripping was replaced by the SynthStrip brain mask, resampled to FreeSurfer's conformed grid. Gray-matter, cortical-ribbon, and subcortical masks were derived from the FreeSurfer segmentation labels. White, pial, midthickness, and inflated surfaces and spherical registrations were exported to GIFTI with Connectome Workbench \citep{marcus2011workbench}. The fsaverage6 template geometry (40,962 vertices per hemisphere) was obtained from TemplateFlow \citep{ciric2022templateflow}.

\subsubsection*{Spatial normalization}

The T1w reference was registered nonlinearly to the MNI152NLin2009cAsym template \citep{fonov2011mni} with ANTs \citep{avants2011ants}. Rigid and affine stages used a mutual-information metric, and a final symmetric normalization (SyN) stage \citep{avants2008syn} used a cross-correlation metric. All stages used brain masks.

\subsection*{Functional preprocessing}

\subsubsection*{Overview}

Each BOLD run was preprocessed once and published in the MNI152NLin2009cAsym, T1w, fsaverage6, and fsnative spaces. Slice-timing correction was not performed.

\subsubsection*{Simultaneous-slice artifact correction}

Signal shared among simultaneously acquired slices was estimated and removed in native scanner space with Multiband Artifact Regression in Simultaneous Slices (MARSS) \citep{tubiolo2024marss} for runs with a multiband acceleration factor of 6 or greater. The correction preceded all other processing.

\subsubsection*{Gradient correction and head motion}

BOLD, single-band reference (SBRef), and spin-echo images were corrected for gradient nonlinearity with the HCP gradient-unwarping procedure \citep{glasser2013minimal} when a site gradient profile matched the acquisition and its metadata did not report prior correction. The BOLD displacement field was applied within the single final resampling. Head motion was estimated with FSL MCFLIRT \citep{jenkinson2002mcflirt}. A matched SBRef served as the registration reference when it passed metadata, pose, overlap, and similarity checks; otherwise a BOLD-derived reference was used.

\subsubsection*{Susceptibility distortion correction}

Susceptibility distortion was estimated with the first applicable method: FSL TOPUP \citep{andersson2003topup} with an opposite-phase-encoding spin-echo fieldmap pair; otherwise SynBOLD-DisCo \citep{yu2023synbold}, which synthesizes an undistorted BOLD reference from the T1w image for TOPUP; and otherwise nonlinear registration of the BOLD reference to the T1w anatomy with ANTs SyN \citep{avants2008syn}.

\subsubsection*{Anatomical registration}

The distortion-corrected BOLD reference was aligned to the T1w anatomy with FreeSurfer boundary-based registration \citep{greve2009bbr}, using the white surface, coreg initialization, and 6 degrees of freedom.

\subsubsection*{Resampling}

Per-frame motion, distortion, and anatomical transforms were composed and applied in a single interpolation with AFNI \emph{3dNwarpApply} \citep{cox1996afni}, using wsinc5 interpolation for the signal and linear interpolation for the warps. Template-space outputs used the T1w-to-template transforms from anatomical preprocessing. Volumes were written on an anatomically oriented grid at the BOLD voxel size. Surface time series were sampled within the cortical ribbon between the white and pial surfaces with Connectome Workbench \citep{marcus2011workbench}.

\subsubsection*{Confounds and outlier frames}

Confound time series included the six rigid-body motion parameters; global, white-matter, and cerebrospinal-fluid signals; the temporal derivatives and quadratic terms of these signals \citep{satterthwaite2013confound}; framewise displacement (FD) \citep{power2012spurious} computed with a 50 mm head radius; 10 anatomical CompCor components from combined white-matter and cerebrospinal-fluid voxels \citep{behzadi2007compcor}; DVARS; and discrete cosine drift regressors with a 0.0078125 Hz (128 s) cutoff.

Frames were marked as outliers when FD exceeded 1 mm or when DVARS met both the statistical criterion (one-sided test at a 5\% Bonferroni-corrected family-wise error rate) and the practical criterion (change in percent D-var greater than 5\%) of \citet{afyouni2018dvars}. Up to 20 initial non-steady-state volumes were also marked.

\subsection*{Denoising}

\subsubsection*{Nuisance regression and filtering}

Runs with fewer than 50 frames were excluded. When the smoothing FWHM was positive, data were smoothed with Connectome Workbench \citep{marcus2011workbench} in the surface or volume geometry before temporal modeling, and volumetric smoothing was restricted to a gray-matter mask thresholded at 0.2.

Frames marked by any outlier column were censored: they were excluded from model fitting, and their output values are model reconstructions. Nuisance regressors were the mean cerebral-cortex signal, averaged over FreeSurfer cortical voxels after scaling each voxel to unit variance, FD, the six rigid-body motion parameters, the first five anatomical CompCor components, and the cosine drift terms. A real Fourier basis spanning 0.01 to 0.1 Hz was constructed, together with task regressors where events were available and detrending terms. On retained frames, nuisance regressors were projected into this passband, orthogonalized with respect to the task and detrending terms, standardized, and reduced by principal component analysis to the fewest components explaining 99\% of their variance. At least 30 dimensions and 50\% of the passband rank were left after nuisance removal, and nuisance regression was skipped when fewer than 30 dimensions remained before it. Each BOLD series was fitted to the remaining passband basis on retained frames and reconstructed at every frame, then standardized with the mean and standard deviation of retained frames.

\subsection*{Dynamic connectivity}

\subsubsection*{Connectivity pooling}

Cleaned runs were pooled within each participant, space, and smoothing level. A run was included if cleaning was defined, at least 100 frames and 70\% of its frames were retained, the cleaning model left at least 50 residual degrees of freedom, the participation effective rank of the cleaned data was at least 10, and no single temporal component explained more than 50\% of its variance. Each participant required at least 1 usable run and 100 retained frames in total.

Censored frames were omitted, and each admitted run was centered and standardized at every spatial location before pooling. Each run's contribution to the pooled covariance was weighted in proportion to the temporal degrees of freedom remaining after cleaning. The leading eigenspace of the weighted, pooled correlation matrix was estimated with a streamed randomized decomposition \citep{halko2011randomized} of at most 1000 dimensions, with an oversampling of 16 and 1 power iteration, without forming the full location-by-location matrix. The fit was represented as a short synthetic series whose sample correlations reproduce the fitted low-rank correlation matrix, for seed-based connectivity in Connectome Workbench \citep{marcus2011workbench}.

\subsection*{Individualized networks}

\subsubsection*{Individualized network estimation}

Each participant's pooled connectivity series formed a matrix with one row per spatial location and one column per fitted low-rank dimension. When it had more than 1000 columns, it was projected onto its leading 1000 randomized singular vectors \citep{halko2011randomized} with an oversampling of 10 and 2 power iterations.

Spatial independent component analysis with FastICA \citep{hyvarinen1999fastica}, as implemented in scikit-learn \citep{pedregosa2011sklearn}, decomposed this matrix into 100 components, treating locations as observations, with unit-variance whitening, at most 500 iterations, and a tolerance of 0.0001. Each component was oriented so that its median loading was nonpositive. Each network map was the correlation between every location and the oriented component's time course, signed to agree with the component's loadings. The correlations were not rescaled or thresholded. These maps are not calibrated probabilities and are not normalized across networks.

\subsubsection*{Network labeling}

Networks were given heuristic labels by spatial correspondence with population reference maps: the 15 networks of \citet{du2024organization} and the probabilistic language atlas of \citet{lipkin2022probabilistic}. Each reference map was projected into the participant's target geometry and correlated spatially with every network map. For each reference, the 3 most correlated networks received its label, in rank order, so a network could receive several labels. Networks that no reference selected kept numeric identifiers. These labels describe spatial similarity and are not functional localizer results.
